target_customer: Companies running large Linux endpoint fleets such as GPU clusters, cloud devices and on-device deployments
problem: OS level vulnerabilities take weeks to patch across fleets. Palisade monitors kernel level signals, finds vulnerabilities and applies fixes across endpoints in minutes.
product_category: Kernel level runtime security and automated remediation

founders.name: Fnu Prince
education: Left Caltech at 18 to start the company (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says red team and blue team security work from age 16 and olympiad results; no employers named.

competitors.name: Falco
competitors.what: CNCF graduated open source runtime security
competitors.traction_then: called a de facto standard in 2026 overviews

competitors.name: Tetragon
competitors.what: Cilium sub project using eBPF to enforce runtime policy

competitors.name: Upwind
competitors.what: Runtime cloud security built on eBPF data
competitors.traction_then: named Strong Visionary Leader in a 2026 analyst radar

technical_complexity.rationale: Kernel level monitoring with LSM-BPF and safe automated fixes across fleets is hard, and a mistake can crash endpoints.

defensibility.rationale: Kernel expertise is scarce, but open source tools and funded vendors cover detection; automated fixing is the differentiator and unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Detection incumbents exist; no one found doing automated patching from eBPF signals, and no action against Palisade found.

market_need_then: Linux admins were shifting to kernel level runtime visibility in 2026 and eBPF has known attack surface, per security sources; the company's own CVE handling claims are unverified.

branding.domain_note: Uses palisade-ai.com with an AI suffix because palisade.com belongs to another company.

brand_strength.rationale: Palisade Research, Highflame's Palisade and others share the name, so searches return unrelated entities.

outcome_analysis: Palisade is a one person Summer 2026 security startup with deep technical ambition and no disclosed funding, exit or layoff. It faces confusable naming and established runtime security vendors, but offers automated remediation that others lack. Outcome is open and no factors are assigned.
notes: No funding found. Palisade Research (AI safety nonprofit) and Highflame's Palisade model scanner are different entities. YC launch post claims it already handles two named CVEs; unverified.
